title: Region probe + soft-quarantine with eviction-delay fastpatch
author: Leah Chen
release_notes: Hotpatch: Introduce regional probe weighting and a soft-quarantine path with delayed local eviction to reduce SLO blips during transient network/egress issues. No breaking changes. Backported conservative defaults to release branch.
description:
Context: Over the past two weeks we've observed short-lived regional latency spikes that caused transient SLO violations for high-priority tenants. Root cause analysis pointed to a combination of (1) aggressive local KV-cache eviction during transient errors, (2) immediate hard circuit-open on single-region probe failures, and (3) downstream routing that immediately directed traffic to slow cold-paths, amplifying tail latency. This PR implements a low-risk fastpatch that reduces SLO noise while preserving safety and is intended as an emergency mitigation ahead of a larger rework.

What this changes (high level):
- Add a region health probe with weighted tenant scoring: probes now aggregate short-window percentiles and tenant-impact weights to decide probation state instead of binary fail-once logic.
- Introduce soft-quarantine state (soft-open) for circuits: region is marked probationary and routed with reduced traffic share and increased sampling rather than fully tripped. Allows gradual failover versus immediate hard eject.
- Eviction-delay for local KV caches: when a region enters probation, eviction of prefetched/kv entries is delayed by a small, configurable window to avoid cold-cache storms.
- Persistent circuit metadata store: circuit state and soft-quarantine counters persisted to Redis with compact TTL so state survives controller restarts and prevents rapid flip-flopping.
- Lightweight routing shim: new policy favors immediate cross-region hedging only for traffic above a latency-sensitive threshold; lower-priority requests continue to use region but with caution flags.
- Feature flags and conservative defaults: all behavioral changes are behind runtime flags and default to conservative thresholds to minimize customer impact.

Why this is safe: The implementation is additive; default runtime flags keep behavior unchanged. The soft-quarantine reduces the chance of mass cold-cache invalidation by avoiding immediate eviction and hard routing changes. Persistence TTLs are short (minutes) and can be tuned by ops.

Commits (summary):
- 9c1a2d3: add region probe aggregation and weighting logic
- 5b2f8e0: soft-quarantine state machine and routing adjustments
- e7d4f11: delay-based eviction strategy and unit tests
- a4b9c0d: redis-backed circuit metadata persistence
- d3f1b2a: add feature flags, integration tests, and docs/ops notes

Files touched (high-level):
- src/scheduler/region_probe.go (new aggregator + metrics)
- src/runtime/circuit_soft_open.go (soft-quarantine state machine)
- src/runtime/kv_eviction_delay.go (eviction delay implementation)
- src/infra/redis_store.go (compact TTL helpers + tests)
- src/proxy/routing_policy.go (hedged routing shim)
- docs/ops/region-quarantine.md (runbook + flags)
- tests/integration/probe_soft_quarantine_test.go
- helm/templates/values.yaml (defaults + feature flags)

Review conversation (excerpt):
- Marco Ruiz (request_changes): "Two concerns: (1) persisting circuit state to Redis adds an operational dependency; we need circuit TTLs and a fallback if Redis is degraded. (2) Need a clearer metric that shows %traffic actually hedged so SRE can validate effectiveness."
- Author (Leah): "Addressed: added a Redis circuit fallback to local-memory with exponential backoff and added probe_hedge_ratio metric. Updated tests to simulate Redis outage. See commit a4b9c0d and d3f1b2a."
- Samir Kapoor (comment): "Eviction delay looks good but let's ensure it can't cause memory blowup under pathological workloads; suggest guard rails."
- Author (Leah): "Added an eviction-cap soft-limit and forced immediate trim if memory pressure crosses a configured threshold. Added benchmark note to docs."
- Janelle Ortiz (approve): "Verified integration tests and the hedged routing metric in staging traces. Approving for squash-merge to main; recommend backport to release branch."

CI and validation:
- CI pipeline: lint -> unit tests -> integration (k8s kind) -> e2e shadow run on staging. Initial run failed integration (timeout in probe test), fixed by increasing probe timeouts (commit e7d4f11). Final CI: all checks passed. Post-merge staging shadow run showed 43% reduction in SLO noise for a known incident window (sample day).

Rollout plan:
1) Merge to main via squash.
2) Immediately enable feature flag in staging for 24h smoke tests.
3) Roll to production for 10% of tenants for 2 hours, monitor probe_hedge_ratio, region_probation_count, eviction_delay_trims, and memory pressure gauges.
4) If stable, increase to 50% then full rollout. Ops will keep the conservative defaults live and can tune via flags.

Post-merge notes / Ops runbook snippet:
- Flag keys: runtime.enable_soft_quarantine (boolean), runtime.eviction_delay_ms (int), runtime.eviction_cap_mb (int).
- Quick rollback: disable runtime.enable_soft_quarantine. If Redis outage suspected, set runtime.redis_circuit_fallback=local.

Merge: Squash-merged to main by Janelle Ortiz on 2026-02-18 after approvals and green CI. Backport PR to release branch created (cherry-pick) and applied with conservative defaults.

Counters and follow-ups:
- Follow-up: ENG-8799 (observability: add per-tenant SLO delta metric tied to probe decisions).
- Follow-up: SRE-1312 (test scalability of eviction-delay under high-tenant cardinality).

This PR is intentionally scoped as an operational fastpatch to reduce immediate customer exposure while giving the team time to design a more comprehensive regional failover rework.
